name: Revit MEP (route, connect, circuits, hangers)
description: Data-driven MEP for a live Revit session: route pipes and ducts with fittings, connect connectors, make electrical circuits, plan and place hangers, and check first that a family really is MEP for the system. check_elements and hanger_plan are read-only. route, connect, circuit and hanger_place are write tools: they need an approved plan, refuse a family whose category or connectors do not match before changing anything, use one transaction per step and roll back on failure unless on_error is skip. Hanger spacing comes only from a table you fill in with named sources; layout aid, not an engineering calculation. Not yet run against a live Revit. Every write tool takes dry_run: it runs the call, reports what would change and rolls it all back (still approval-gated).
author: AEC Model Bridge

commands.title: Dry run of the category guard: say whether elements would be accepted for a pipe, duct or electrical system, and why not (wrong category, no connectors, wrong domain, wrong system, no free connector). Read-only. Use it before revit_mep_route, revit_mep_connect or revit_mep_circuit; for a family that is not placed yet use revit_probe_family.

kind.description: Domain to check against: pipe, duct or elec.

system.description: System the elements must have a connector of. Pipe: hsup, hret, cold, hot, san, vent (or a Revit name such as SupplyHydronic, DomesticColdWater, Sanitary). Duct: supply, return, exhaust, outdoor (or a Revit name such as SupplyAir, ReturnAir, ExhaustAir, OtherAir). Elec: power, data (or PowerCircuit, Data). Omit to check only category and domain.

element_id.description: ElementId (integer) of the family instance. Give element_id or mark.

mark.description: Mark parameter of the family instance; it must belong to exactly one element. Give mark or element_id.

need_free.description: Also require a free (unconnected) connector of the system. Default false.

commands.title: Run pipe or duct between connectors or points, or branch it off a trunk, with elbows, unions, transitions, takeoffs and tees. Use revit_mep_connect when the ends already touch; use this when pipe or duct has to be drawn. Families that are not MEP for the system are refused before anything changes. Write tool: replaces only what it made under the same tag and id; rolls back on failure unless on_error is skip.

tag.description: Your own label for this build phase (for example MEP1). Elements made under the same tag and id are replaced when you run the call again; elements this tool did not make are never touched.

system.description: System to route. Pipe: hsup, hret, cold, hot, san, vent (or a Revit name such as SupplyHydronic, DomesticColdWater, Sanitary). Duct: supply, return, exhaust, outdoor (or a Revit name such as SupplyAir, ReturnAir, ExhaustAir, OtherAir). A system of the other domain is refused.

type_name.description: Pipe or duct type name to use (the type's name in the project). A route can override it.

system_type_name.description: Only for a route that starts at a free point: name of the piping or mechanical system type to use. Default: the first system type of the system's class.

transition_m.description: Distance from a corner at which a size change is placed, metres (default 0.15).

id.description: Your name for this route, unique in the call (letters, digits, _ - .). Used to replace it on a rerun and to branch off it.

level.description: Name of the level the route belongs to; run_height_m and point heights are measured from it.

run_height_m.description: Height of the horizontal run above the level, in metres. Required, except for a branch (it runs at the trunk's height).

size.description: Size of the pipe or duct: diameter_mm, or width_mm with height_mm for a rectangular duct.

diameter_mm.description: Round pipe or duct diameter in millimetres.

width_mm.description: Rectangular duct width in millimetres (with height_mm).

height_mm.description: Rectangular duct height in millimetres (with width_mm).

stub_m.description: Length of the straight stub leaving a connector, in metres (default 0.2).

type_name.description: Pipe or duct type name for this route; overrides the call's type_name.

from.description: A connector of a placed family (element_id or mark, with optional filters) or a free point (point_m).

mark.description: Mark parameter of the family instance; it must belong to exactly one element. Give mark or element_id.

diameter_mm.description: Only connectors whose diameter is between [low, high] millimetres (round connectors), for example [38, 42].

sort.description: Order the matching connectors by this coordinate before index picks one.

index.description: Which of the matching connectors to use after sorting (0 is the first). In a route, connectors used by an earlier route of the same call are skipped.

point_m.description: Instead of a connector: a free point [x, y, height]. x and y are model coordinates in metres; height is metres above the route's level.

to.description: Where the route ends: a connector or a free point. Give to or branch_to, not both.

branch_to.description: End the route on a straight horizontal trunk piece instead of at a connector.

route.description: Id of a trunk route built earlier in this call, or earlier with the same tag.

items.description: ElementId of a pipe or duct.

element_ids.description: Existing pipes or ducts to branch off (takeoff only). Give route or element_ids.

fitting.description: takeoff (default): takeoff fitting on the trunk, trunk unchanged. tee: the trunk piece is split and a tee placed (the trunk must be a route of this tool).

items.description: A corner of the route. The run goes along x first, then y. A size here changes the size from this corner on, with a transition.

to_height_m.description: Optional: also move vertically at this corner to this height above the level (metres).

level.description: Level the to_height_m is measured from (default: the route's level).

via.description: Corner points between from and to, in order. Not for branches.

routes.description: The routes to make (1 to 25), built in this order; a branch may name an earlier route as its trunk.

on_error.description: abort (default): the first failure rolls the whole call back and nothing is kept. skip: keep what worked and list the failures.

dry_run.description: Default false. true: do the whole call inside Revit exactly as normal (same checks, same post-checks), then roll everything back. The result says dry_run true, committed false and what would change (would_change); changed_ids stays empty. Still needs an approved plan like any write. Use it to test a call before the real one.

commands.title: Join pairs of connectors that already touch (equipment to a pipe or duct end, or two pipe or duct ends) directly or with a union, transition or elbow, then list the open ends left. Use revit_mep_route to draw pipe or duct between connectors that are apart. Write tool: needs an approved plan; rolls back on failure unless on_error is skip.

tolerance_mm.description: How far apart two connectors may be and still count as touching, millimetres (default 5).

commands.title: Make native electrical circuits (ElectricalSystem) from a list of placed elements and a panel. Use after the families are placed; a circuit is replaced when you run it again with the same tag and id. Elements already on a circuit this tool did not make are refused; run revit_mep_check_elements first to see whether the families qualify. Write tool: needs an approved plan; rolls back on failure unless on_error is skip.

tag.description: Your own label for this build phase (for example MEP1). Elements made under the same tag and id are replaced when you run the call again; elements this tool did not make are never touched.

system.description: Electrical system type: power (default), data, or a Revit name such as PowerCircuit. A pipe or duct system is refused.

id.description: Your name for this circuit, unique in the call. Used to replace it on a rerun.

name.description: Load Name of the circuit in Revit (default: the id).

panel.description: The panel (an Electrical Equipment family): element_id or mark.

element_id.description: ElementId (integer) of the family instance. Give element_id or mark.

mark.description: Mark parameter of the family instance; it must belong to exactly one element. Give mark or element_id.

element_id.description: ElementId (integer) of the family instance. Give element_id or mark.

mark.description: Mark parameter of the family instance; it must belong to exactly one element. Give mark or element_id.

elements.description: Elements on the circuit (1 to 200): lights, sockets, equipment with an electrical connector.

commands.title: Plan hanger positions along straight pipes, ducts and cable trays: spread at the maximum spacing of a rule you supplied (a rule needs a named source, otherwise 'no spacing rule'), no closer to fittings than a minimum distance, with the floor, beam or ceiling above each position and the rod length, or 'no support host'. A layout aid, not an engineering calculation. Read-only; then place them with revit_mep_hanger_place.

categories.description: Which runs to plan: pipes, ducts, cabletrays. Default all three.

items.description: ElementId (integer) of a pipe, duct or cable tray.

ids.description: Element ids of the runs to plan (at most 2000). Scope: give ids, system, level or view_id; the whole model is never scanned unasked.

system.description: Only runs whose system name contains this text (for example the name of the piping system), case ignored. Scope.

level.description: Only runs whose reference level has this exact name. Scope. List levels with revit_list_levels.

view_id.description: Only runs visible in this view (ElementId of a plan, section or 3D view). Scope.

material.description: Material of the runs in this call, compared without case with the material of each spacing rule. A rule with an empty material matches any material. Default empty.

items.description: One spacing rule. A rule is used only when it names a source and a max_spacing_mm and example is not true.

id.description: Your name for the rule, unique in the list (letters, digits, _ - .).

material.description: Material the rule covers; empty means any.

size_min_mm.description: Smallest nominal diameter (pipe, round duct) or width (rectangular duct, cable tray), millimetres.

max_spacing_mm.description: Largest distance between two hangers on a straight run, millimetres.

min_fitting_distance_mm.description: Nearest a hanger may be to a fitting, millimetres. The call's min_fitting_distance_mm overrides it.

source.description: Required. The standard, supplier table or project document the numbers come from, with clause or page.

example.description: true marks a row that only shows the layout; it is never used.

spacing_rules.description: Spacing rules for this call, used instead of the shipped table (at most 500). Spacing comes only from the rules in conventions/hanger_spacing.json (shipped empty except an example row) or from spacing_rules. A rule without a source text is never used.

min_fitting_distance_mm.description: Nearest a hanger may be to a fitting, millimetres. Overrides the rule's value. Default: the rule's value, else 100 (a layout clearance, not an engineering value).

host_categories.description: What counts as a support host above a hanger: floors, structuralframing (beams), ceilings. Default floors and structuralframing.

include_links.description: Also search loaded linked models for a support host. Default true.

max_reach_mm.description: How far above the top of a run a host is looked for, millimetres (100 to 20000). Default 3000. Beyond it the position is 'no support host'.

max_elements.description: Most runs examined (1 to 2000). Default 500. More runs in scope: the result is truncated.

time_budget_s.description: Seconds after which the work stops and the result is marked truncated (1 to 25). Default 15.

max_hangers.description: Most hangers computed (1 to 3000). Default 1000. Beyond it the result is truncated.

offset.description: Runs to skip, to read the next page. Default 0.

commands.title: Place a loaded hanger family at hanger positions: planned from a scope with the same rules as revit_mep_hanger_plan, or taken from its positions. Skips positions that already have a hanger of the family, so a rerun adds nothing; refuses a family in the wrong category or with MEP connectors; reads every hanger back. Write tool: needs an approved plan; rolls back on failure unless on_error is skip. Layout aid, not an engineering calculation.

items.description: ElementId (integer) of a pipe, duct or cable tray.

ids.description: Plan from these runs (at most 2000) and place the result. Scope: give ids, system, level or view_id, or give hangers instead.

system.description: Only runs whose system name contains this text (for example the name of the piping system), case ignored. Scope.

level.description: Only runs whose reference level has this exact name. Scope. List levels with revit_list_levels.

tag.description: Your own label for this batch (for example HANG1). Each hanger carries it, so a rerun with the same tag skips what it already placed; hangers this tool did not make are never touched.

family_name.description: Name of the loaded hanger family. It must be level based, in Generic Models, Pipe Accessories, Duct Accessories, Cable Tray Fittings or Specialty Equipment, and have no MEP connectors.

type_name.description: Name of the family type to place.

items.description: One position, as returned in positions by revit_mep_hanger_plan, plus the run id.

run_id.description: ElementId of the pipe, duct or cable tray the position lies on.

x_m.description: X in metres, model internal coordinates.

rod_mm.description: Rod length in millimetres, written to rod_length_parameter. Optional.

support.description: The support value from the plan. A position whose support is 'no support host' or 'host_unknown' is skipped unless place_without_host is true.

hangers.description: Positions to place (1 to 500), taken from revit_mep_hanger_plan, instead of a scope. Each must lie on its run within 25 mm.

rod_length_parameter.description: Name of an instance length parameter of the family that receives the rod length in millimetres. Optional; the family is refused when it lacks it.

place_without_host.description: Also place hangers where no support host was found. Default false: those positions are skipped and listed.

existing_tolerance_mm.description: A position with a hanger of this family type within this distance, millimetres, counts as already placed and is skipped (1 to 1000). Default 50.

align_to_run.description: Rotate each hanger about the vertical so the family's X axis follows the run. Default true.

max_hangers.description: Most hangers placed in one call (1 to 500). Default 200. A larger call is refused before anything changes.
